preregistration: P-ROR, frozen 2026-10-30T07:56:05Z. The regime claim compares TGMS on demand (check, then refresh only when flagged) with a maintained view; it lacks the obvious third configuration, *recompute on read*: every read artifact's plan is re-run and republished unconditionally, no lineage check, always exact. Measure it on the on-demand protocol of P-AXES axis B (one correction per burst, k reads drawn uniformly, same stores and k grids, N = 10^3 both stores and the probe; Memgraph stopped, box quiet; code = the pushed tip after lane T19), timed as the same interval. For every TGMS configuration report two timer scopes: reads only (as on record) and reads plus applying the correction (the log append; the scope Table 1 uses for the view), and both median and mean. Predictions: (1) recompute-on-read's cost per read equals the per-artifact refresh on record within 30 % (15.3 synth / 3.4 collegemsg / 15.65 probe ms); (2) at k = N TGMS on demand is cheaper per read by >= 2x on synth 10^3 and the probe (6.30 / 10.56 ms on record) and >= 2.5x on collegemsg (0.93 ms); (3) at k = 1 recompute-on-read is cheaper on collegemsg (~3.4 vs 4.9 ms) and TGMS is cheaper on synth (4.9 vs ~15.3); (4) against the view (median basis) recompute-on-read's crossover is ~7 on synth 10^3, ~1.8 on collegemsg and ~340 on the probe, so lineage extends the regime by >= 2.5x on synth 10^3, >= 1.5x on the probe, and by less than 1.5x on collegemsg. Falsifier: TGMS on demand costs at least as much as recompute-on-read at every measured k on either synth size.
